# First blink in Wokwi: the exercise

<!-- Generated by tools/maintainer/build_exercise_readmes.py from the lesson page. Edit the lesson, then run the script. -->

Lesson: [First blink in Wokwi](https://jouhis.github.io/embedded-course/lessons/0002-first-blink-in-wokwi.html). Read it first: the steps below refer to its diagrams and worked examples.

## Try it in Wokwi

The starter runs the template blink unchanged, at 1 Hz with the on-board LED on for 500 ms and off for 500 ms. Its comments mark two tasks; look for the comments tagged `(learner)` in `main.c`.

1. **Task 1: make the blink 5 Hz.** 5 Hz means 100 ms on and 100 ms off. Change the two `sleep_ms` delays in `main.c` from 500 to 100, build with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>B</kbd> and start the simulator. **Expected output:** the on-board LED blinks five times per second, and the serial monitor prints `LED on` and `LED off` alternately, about ten lines per second. The lines scroll quickly, so judge the timing from the LED rather than the text.
2. **Task 2: add an external LED.** Add a `wokwi-led` part and a `wokwi-resistor` part to `diagram.json`. Wire the LED's anode (pin `A`) to `GP15`, the LED's cathode (pin `C`) to resistor pin `1`, and resistor pin `2` to `GND.1`. Set the resistor's `value` attribute to `"220"`, meaning 220 Ω. Each connection is a line like `["pico:GP15", "led1:A", "green", []]`. Save the file, then build and start the simulator again.
3. **Change the code for the external LED.** Declare a constant `EXT_LED_PIN` with the value 15, and add `gpio_init` and `gpio_set_dir(EXT_LED_PIN, GPIO_OUT)` next to the existing pair. In the loop, write the opposite level to the external pin each time you write the on-board pin. Build again.
4. **Run and observe.** Before you start the simulator, predict what the two LEDs should do. **Expected output:** they take turns five times per second each, so when one is lit the other is dark, and the serial monitor shows the blink lines. The reference solution prints `Blink 5 Hz: on-board on, external off` and `Blink 5 Hz: on-board off, external on`, which makes the phases easy to check.

The resistor limits the current through the LED. Lesson 9 shows how to choose its value, so the exact number can wait.

- `diagram.json`

## Done when

The serial monitor prints `Blink 5 Hz: on-board on, external off`.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint for the wiring</summary>

Part types and pin names are on the [Wokwi LED page](https://docs.wokwi.com/parts/wokwi-led) and the [Wokwi resistor page](https://docs.wokwi.com/parts/wokwi-resistor). If the simulator starts with the LED dark, check the anode and cathode first: the anode belongs on the pin side.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint for the timing</summary>

A period is the time for one complete on-and-off cycle. 100 ms on plus 100 ms off makes 200 ms, and frequency is the inverse of the period: 1 ÷ 0.2 s = 5 Hz.

</details>
